page.layout: Running head at top centre; page number top right. Two medallion engravings (Leo Armenius left, Michael Balbus right) above the text. Below them one column of running text in two paragraphs.

main_text.l: LEO Armenius, huius nominis Constantinopolis Impera-
tor quintus, ac post Carolum magnum Romanorum Imperatorem,
quartus à Nicephoro, dum in oriente Michaëlis supradicti Im-
peratoris Duce agit, ad imperium aspirans seditione in exerci-
tu excitat, factúsque est à militibus Imperator ann. mun. 4775.
à Christo nato 813. hic vbi regiâ ingressus est, Michaëlis filium
abscissis genitalibus in exilium misit. victoriam de Bulgaris retu-
lit, Thraciâ recuperauit, quàm plurimos hostes cepit, repressi-
tque eorum audaces conatus, qui iam Adrianopoli potiti, in Con-
stantinopolim arma meditabatur. Diuorum imagines quas fu-
stulerat ipse, cum nollet restituere, noctu per insidias dū sacris
operatur, in ipso templo ab imaginum cultoribus capite trunca-
tur, ac multis confoditur vulneribus, anno imperij octauo: vxor
in monasterium truditur, filij in exilium pelluntur. Vide Egn.
lib.2. ac Cosmographiam Munsteri lib.4. & Blond.
MICHAEL Balbus prauissimis moribus imbutus, qúeque
Leonē prædictum confoderat, imperat Constantinopoli anno
mundi 4783. à Christo nato 821. Hic humili ac sordido loco
natus, Thomam virum quidem obscurum, qui tyrannidē inua-
serat, vario primùm rerum euentu aggressus, tandem oppressit:
cùm prius eò desperationis deductus esset, vt ex arce Constan-
tini ad Peram, oppidulum, ferreā catenā produxisset. Itaque
traditum sibi Thomā, qui Adrianopolim se receperat, manibus
pedibúsq; truncauit, multisque cruciatibus affectum, tandè iu-
gulauit. Saraceni hoc principe Cretam occupant, totámq; ferè
in ditionē redigunt, Græcos duplici vincunt prælio. Obiit Mi-
chaël vētris profluuio anno imperij nono. Vetus oraculum in-
notuit, tum rem Romanam ruitura, cùm & Balbus & auarissimus prin-
ceps imperaret. Vide vt supra.

page.notes: Two medallion engravings above the text carry legends: left "LEO ARMENIVS" (partly cut off at the left edge, "...NIVS" and "LEO ARM..."), right "MICHAEL BALBVS" (partly cut off, "BALBVS" and "MICHAEL"). These are part of the illustrations and are not transcribed as text. Printed "ann .mun." has a stray space, left as printed. The "dū" in "per insidias dū sacris" is uncertain (the mark over the u may be a macron or a tilde), so it could be "dū" or "dum": [?] not added because the reading is clear enough in context.
